mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation issued by the New Zealand Registrar of Companies
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (Registrar of Companies)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a notary public in the source jurisdiction, followed exclusively by either (i) a Hague Apostille certificate issued by the source jurisdiction's designated competent authority where the source country is an Apostille Convention member, or (ii) consular legalization by the New Zealand Embassy/High Commission/Consulate with jurisdiction over the source country where the source country is not an Apostille Convention member. The two authentication paths are parallel and mutually exclusive; they may never be applied sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Incorporation Status from the New Zealand Companies Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (Registrar of Companies)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a notary public in the source jurisdiction, followed exclusively by either (i) Hague Apostille for Apostille Convention source states, or (ii) consular legalization via the New Zealand diplomatic mission competent for the source state for non-Apostille states. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive; no sequential chaining is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney appointing the first director, local registered office agent, and banking signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Subscriber board / founding incorporator executing under Companies Act 1993, Schedule 1 or the company's proposed constitution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in the country of execution; if the executing country is an Apostille Convention member, attach a Hague Apostille from that country's competent authority; if the executing country is not an Apostille Convention member, complete consular legalization at the New Zealand Embassy or Consulate that covers the executing country. These two routes are alternative, never cumulative.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Corporate Constitution (proposed during pre-incorporation and circulated for regulatory review)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporators/shareholders of NZ LTD in accordance with Companies Act 1993, sections 30-36
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of the introductory execution page, then either apostille (if the subscribing entity's home jurisdiction is an Apostille party) or consular legalization at the New Zealand diplomatic post in the home jurisdiction (if not an Apostille party). The two authentication streams are exhaustive alternatives and must not be combined sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter / Confirmation of Directorship and Signature Specimen from a New Zealand or highly regarded international bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand authorized bank or an acceptable foreign financial institution whose AML/KYC standard is at least equivalent to the New Zealand banking code of practice
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank letter must bear a wet-ink authorized signature and bank seal, be notarized, and then be authenticated by a single exclusive path: Hague Apostille if the bank's country is an Apostille Convention member, or consular legalization at the New Zealand Embassy/Consulate with responsibility for that country if the bank's country is not an Apostille Convention member. No apostille-consular chain is recognized.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, authorized signatories, and any beneficial controller with 25% or greater interest against: (1) the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit watchlists and domestic sanctions maintained under the United Nations Act 1946 and Russia Sanctions Act 2022; (2) the consolidated United Nations Security Council sanctions and terrorist designation lists; (3) the United States OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List and Non-SDN Lists; (4) Her Majesty's Treasury consolidated UK sanctions lists; and (5) the Financial Markets Authority enforcement and disqualification registers. PEP determinations must cover domestic and foreign PEPs, their family members, and close associates using automated name-matching, phonetic fuzzy logic, negative news screening, and source-of-funds verification. Screening must be refreshed at onboarding, quarterly, and immediately before adverse-material events; any PEP flag or ambiguity triggers enhanced due diligence with escalation to the AML compliance committee.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office Name Reservation Service and Companies Register online portal (companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz / the New Zealand Business Number 'NZBN' integrated name-approval gateway)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be expressed in English or te reo Māori using Latin-script characters, with Māori macrons permitted. Chinese characters, any non-Latin script, Arabic diacritics, or CJK glyphs are not accepted in the legal name field; if a foreign-language trade name is desired it must be phonetically transliterated into English letters and, if used in China or other non-English jurisdictions, separately registered as a non-legal trade name. The Registrar applies a four-tier naming doctrine: Tier 1 legal element (must end in 'Limited' or 'Ltd'); Tier 2 distinctive element that is unique and not misleading; Tier 3 descriptive industry element limited to a maximum of two words except where required to define ISIC 6201 software scope; Tier 4 prohibited or sensitive token requiring prior ministerial, regulatory, or Crown consent.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 20 working days of a rejection notice, the user should file a reconsideration request in the Companies Office online name-reservation tool, attaching a letter of consent from the relevant minister or regulator if a sensitive token caused the refusal, or submitting evidence of prior use, registrability, and distinctiveness. The holding company's corporate attorney must retain the full Companies Office rejection reference and statutory ground. If the reconsideration is declined, an appeal may be commenced in the High Court of New Zealand under the judicial review procedures of the Judicial Review Procedure Act 2016 no later than 28 working days after the reconsideration decision; interim, a fresh name may be reserved immediately to avoid losing the incorporation timetable. Each rejection must be remediated by a new distinctive token; no appeal suspends the 30-day reservation window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is statutorily tolerated as a registered office location only if it is a genuine street address in New Zealand, accessible for service of process, and staffed or serviced during normal business hours. For the ISIC 6201 vertical ERP/CRM cloud business, Inland Revenue, the Companies Office, and New Zealand banking counterparties will not accept a standalone virtual office as proof of commercial substance for GST registration, bank account opening with Stripe Billing or Direct Debit rails, or tax residency/PE analyses. To mitigate, the company must complement the virtual office with a physical service arrangement, a New Zealand tax-resident director or administrative agent, local books-and-records access, and contemporaneous evidence of economic activity such as software licensing contracts, server procurement, or regional sales support.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) registered office is a residential address or unstaffed virtual suite; (2) all directors/UBOs are non-resident; (3) no New Zealand bank account or GST registration; (4) high value of vertical cloud subscription invoices during first year; (5) Stripe/Direct Debit transaction flow without contractual support; (6) use of a nominee director with no board minutes. Quantified risk of unannounced on-site inspection by Inland Revenue and the Companies Office is 10% annual baseline for a low-risk software veil, rising to 35% if any of the six red flags are present and to 60% if the company applies for GST refunds exceeding NZD 50,000 in the first 12 months.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), especially sections 12, 14, 16, 20, 21, 24, 126, 151, 152, 153, 189 and 191; the Companies Regulations 1994 for prescribed forms and fees; the Financial Reporting Act 2013 for statutory reporting; and the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 for beneficial owner and director verification.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies – New Zealand Companies Office, an agency within the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 3 – Application for Registration of a Company, filed online; Form 2 – Consent to Appointment as Director/Manager; optional Constitution of the Company under sections 21-29 of the Companies Act 1993; and online Companies Office change notices for post-incorporation updates.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the Companies Act 1993; the Company may be incorporated with zero or nominal share capital, no escrow account or blocked capital account is required, and shares may be allotted by the board for a lawful consideration determined by the board, subject to solvency and director duty rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: AT A MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [·] LIMITED (the Company) duly convened and held at [registered office address], New Zealand, on [date] at [time], with all directors present forming a quorum and with no director objecting, the following resolutions were moved, seconded and unanimously passed. 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT. RESOLVED that the initial subscription of ordinary shares described in the application for registration is approved; the consideration, if any, is accepted; the board and any lawfully appointed delegate are authorized to make the return of allotment, to issue securities, and to execute share certificates. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE AND ADDRESS FOR SERVICE. RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company shall be at the physical address filed with the Registrar of Companies in New Zealand, and that the Company shall maintain its share register, register of directors, register of charges, minutes and accounting records at that office, or at another lawful location, as the board may from time to time determine. 3. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. RESOLVED that [name], [name] and [name] are appointed respectively as director, director, and chief financial officer or company secretary, each to serve until replaced by the board; that each appointee consents to act; that the directors shall exercise their duties in accordance with applicable New Zealand law; and that all required consents and changes of officer particulars shall be filed with the Registrar. 4. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED that [name of licensed bank] is appointed as the principal banker of the Company; that corporate bank accounts shall be opened; that the bank mandate shall require any two authorized signatories to sign together for all payments and withdrawals; and that the directors and company secretary are authorized to execute banking mandates, to receive funds, and to settle subscription collection through Stripe Billing and direct debit. 5. REGULATORY AND COMMERCIAL AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED that the directors and any person so appointed by the board are authorized to apply for the certificate of incorporation, to register the Company with the Inland Revenue Department and the New Zealand Companies Office, to execute the constitution, to adopt commercial contracts, to appoint legal counsel and accountants, and to do every lawful act required to commence the vertical cloud ERP/CRM software business. RESOLVED FURTHER that these minutes shall be signed by the chair and entered in the Company minute book; that certified copies of this resolution are conclusive to third parties; and that this Pro-Forma First Board Resolution is binding, effective immediately, and remains effective until varied by a subsequent valid board resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Approval, Address for Service and Initial Director Consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies – New Zealand Companies Office online portal using RealMe login (www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The proposed company name must not be identical or misleadingly similar to an existing or reserved name, and must not contravene section 20 of the Companies Act 1993. The applicant must first perform an online name availability search at the Companies Office website, then file Form 2 or the equivalent online consent to appointment for each proposed director and manager. Each director s full legal name, residential address and date of birth must be entered through the RealMe verified identity system. The applicant should ensure that at least one director is ordinarily resident in New Zealand or Australia, that no director is disqualified, and that the proposed address for service in New Zealand is valid before continuing to the registration application.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and explanatory cover letter if required
Form 2 – Consent to Appointment as Director/Manager
RealMe verified identity for the applicant and each director
Passport or national identity document for each director
Residential address proof for each director, not older than three months
Constitution, if the Company adopts an affirmative constitution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or a consent is queried, respond in writing to the Companies Office within the deadline stated in the query, propose an alternative compliant name under section 20, cure any defective consent signature, and resubmit the online application; if suspension occurs, request reconsideration by the Registrar and provide a statutory declaration confirming the identity and eligibility of the proposed officers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for Registration and Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies – New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment, Online Registration System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using RealMe business login, the applicant must file Form 3 – Application for Registration of a Company, including the approved company name, full director details, registered office physical address in New Zealand, address for service, share class and initial allotment information, and any adopted constitution. The application must be complete before submission because the Registrar verifies compliance with the Companies Act 1993. The currently prescribed online filing fee of NZD 70 must be paid electronically. If the application is accepted, the Companies Office issues the certificate of incorporation electronically. The Company must not trade before incorporation except for pre-registration contracts expressly adopted by the board after incorporation.
required_dossiers: Form 3 – Application for Registration of a Company
Form 2 consents for each proposed director and manager
Signed constitution, if any, with shareholder approval
Registered office physical address in New Zealand, not a PO Box
Address for service in New Zealand
Electronic payment authorization for the NZD 70 filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected or queried, the applicant must read the Registrar s specific objection notice, correct the defective fields or replace any ineligible director, file the required statutory declaration or supporting documents, and resubmit online; if the application remains suspended, request a formal Registrar review and provide evidence of legal capacity and identity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Governance: Statutory Registers, Registered Office Confirmation and Officer Notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office and the Company s own board of directors; officer changes and annual returns are filed online through the Companies Office portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within two working days after the certificate of incorporation is issued, the board must establish the statutory registers, including the register of members, register of directors, register of charges and the minute book. The registered office and address for service must be physically active and capable of receiving legal documents during normal business hours. The first board resolution must be signed by the chair and inserted in the minute book. Any change of registered office, director or officer must be notified to the Companies Office through the online change notice function. The Company must also confirm its New Zealand Business Number and verify that the filed director details match the certificate of incorporation before any customer agreement is executed.
required_dossiers: Electronic certificate of incorporation issued by the Companies Office
Signed first board resolution and minutes
Register of members and share allotment schedule
Register of directors with residential addresses and consent forms
Register of charges, if any
Constitution, if adopted, and certified copy for the Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office records show an inconsistency with the certificate of incorporation, the Company should file the relevant online change notice or apply for a correction of the register; where a filing deadline has been missed, provide a statutory declaration explaining the delay and request restoration or rectification of the records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: IRD Number, GST Registration and Payment Rails Tax Configuration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), New Zealand, through the MyIR business portal and the Companies Office one-stop shop
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, the Company must ensure that an IRD number is active for the new company. If the expected taxable turnover will exceed NZD 60,000 in a twelve-month period, the Company must register for GST and choose an appropriate GST basis such as payments basis, invoice basis or hybrid basis. The IRD profile may be created automatically from the Companies Office data, but the directors must verify the start date and select the correct industry classification for ISIC 6201 computer programming activities. Because subscription fees will be collected through Stripe Billing and direct debit, the Company must issue compliant tax invoices and determine the GST treatment of local and offshore customers. If employees are appointed, PAYE and KiwiSaver registration must also be completed.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and New Zealand Business Number
Company name and registered address as appearing in Companies Office records
IRD number application or confirmation request through MyIR
Forecast annual turnover and intended GST registration date
Bank account details for IRD refunds, if applicable
Employment agreements and PAYE/KiwiSaver details if staff are appointed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD number application is suspended, contact the Inland Revenue Department by secure message, provide the certificate of incorporation and verification of director identity, correct any business classification errors, and re-submit; if a GST registration date is challenged, submit the underlying customer contracts and payment processor statements to prove the commencement of taxable activity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account and Low-Risk Payment Rails Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed New Zealand registered banks, including ANZ, ASB, BNZ or Westpac, and authorized board appointees; Stripe Billing and direct debit providers as non-bank payment service providers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The board must select a licensed New Zealand bank and submit the corporate account application together with the certificate of incorporation, constitution and signed first board resolution appointing signatories. The bank will conduct anti-money-laundering and countering-financing-of-terrorism customer due diligence, requiring proof of identity for all directors and beneficial owners. After the account is active, the Company may execute a merchant services agreement with Stripe Billing and a direct debit scheme agreement for subscription collection. The executed bank mandate must match the payment routing instructions, and no financial services licence is required because the Company is only selling software subscriptions and is not holding customer money. The Company must maintain PCI DSS evidence and renew merchant underwriting data as requested.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and current Companies Office extract
Constitution and signed first board resolution
Directors residential and identity documents
Beneficial ownership declaration for AML/CFT due diligence
Bank mandate form with at least two authorized signatories
Business plan, sample invoice and projected subscription volumes for merchant underwriting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or payment provider requests additional information, promptly deliver the missing beneficial ownership declarations, source-of-funds evidence and business structure diagrams; if the application is declined, request a written AML/CFT risk decision and submit the file to an alternative licensed bank or to Stripe appeals after correcting the business descriptor and processing history.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable – no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing operations exist under ISIC 6201; the Company is a pure digital ERP/CRM vertical cloud software provider, so no industrial licensing board or municipal manufacturing permit is engaged.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable – no statutory operating or manufacturing licence is required for software publishing and cloud subscription services under ISIC 6201 and NAICS 511210; the Company must nonetheless comply with the Privacy Act 2020, the Unsolicited Electronic Messages Act 2007 and the Commerce Commission fair trading rules.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable – the New Zealand Environmental Protection Authority and territorial local councils acting under the Resource Management Act 1991 are not engaged because the Company carries out no land-disturbing, manufacturing, discharge or hazardous-materials activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable – no Environmental Impact Assessment, restricted activity category, or environmental registration trigger arises from vertical cloud software development, customer relationship management services, or subscription billing through Stripe Billing and direct debit.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable – the Company has zero on-site point-source wastewater discharges, zero volatile organic compound emissions and zero hazardous waste handling; any data-centre electricity consumption, hardware lifecycle or e-waste obligations are contractually assigned to cloud infrastructure providers, with adherence to the Waste Minimisation Act 2008 and New Zealand data centre environmental standards to be documented in supplier agreements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for a manufacturing or warehousing fire permit, because the Company operates as a digital software business; however, if the Company occupies commercial premises in New Zealand, the landlord must maintain a current Building Warrant of Fitness and an approved Fire and Emergency New Zealand evacuation scheme, and the Company must comply with the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 for office ergonomics, electrical equipment safety and emergency planning.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of New Zealand; secure online taxpayer portal: myIR at https://myir.ird.govt.nz. Company incorporation and the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) are administered by the Companies Office within the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE); export clearance and customs declarations are administered by the New Zealand Customs Service through the Trade Single Window (TSW).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident investor forming a New Zealand limited company: (1) Incorporate the NZ_LTD entity through the Companies Office online register; the resulting NZBN is the master business identifier and Companies Office data is shared with Inland Revenue, which issues the company's unique IRD number for income tax and Goods and Services Tax (GST) registration. (2) If the foreign entity instead operates as an offshore non-resident company without New Zealand incorporation, apply directly to Inland Revenue for an IRD number through myIR using the non-resident company application route; provide certified constitutional documents, ultimate beneficial ownership information, registered office or service agent details, and a New Zealand address for service, and appoint a New Zealand tax agent if there is no physical presence. (3) To become GST-registered, use the GST registration function in myIR after the IRD number is issued; the applicant must certify that it carries on or intends to carry on a taxable activity in New Zealand and must satisfy the NZD 60,000 registration threshold, or register voluntarily. Provide New Zealand bank account details for GST refunds; a non-resident entity lacking an NZ bank account should arrange a designated account or tax agent trust account for refund purposes. (4) If goods are to be exported, obtain a Customs client code from the New Zealand Customs Service and lodge export entries through TSW. (5) Maintain all documentary evidence in English for IRD and Customs inspection.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand has no check-the-box regime. A standard NZ_LTD is taxed as a separate entity at the corporate income tax rate and may be eligible, if closely held (five or fewer shareholders and no corporate shareholder), to elect Look-Through Company (LTC) status through Inland Revenue; an LTC election makes income tax transparent but is not the default. No elective hybrid-mismatch election exists; New Zealand's hybrid and branch mismatch rules are mandatory anti-avoidance provisions under the Taxation (Neutralising Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Act 2019.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) administered under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in New Zealand in any 12-month period, or expected taxable supplies in the next 12 months; the same NZD 60,000 threshold applies to non-resident suppliers of remote digital services and low-value imported goods selling into New Zealand consumers. Registration below the threshold is voluntary but becomes mandatory once the threshold is exceeded or is likely to be exceeded.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not impose mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, anti-fraud digital stamping, or pre-clearance of invoices with Inland Revenue. GST-registered suppliers must issue tax invoices containing the prescribed particulars (supplier name, GST registration number, invoice date, supplier and recipient details, description, quantity and amount including GST) and retain them for the statutory record-keeping period. E-invoicing is voluntary and implemented under the PEPPOL framework (PEPPOL BIS Billing 3.0); certified PEPPOL access points are used for interoperability with government and trading partners. There is no API-based fiscal pre-clearance obligation for ordinary B2B supplies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 where the supply is an exported good or a qualifying offshore service. Goods must be exported from New Zealand by the supplier in the course of the supplier's taxable activity, or supplied for removal to an outside destination, and must leave New Zealand substantively unchanged within the applicable statutory timeframe. Qualifying offshore digital services, including the vertical ERP CRM cloud software subscriptions in scope, are zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident recipient who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply, and the services have no direct connection with New Zealand land, goods, or a person present in New Zealand and are not consumed in New Zealand. The supplier should retain written contracts, orders, IP access records, and billing showing the offshore customer, overseas contract jurisdiction, delivery of access outside New Zealand, and GST-exclusive export invoices.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs Service export entry (export declaration) lodged through the Trade Single Window and approved by Customs; this statutory export-clearance record is the functional equivalent of a Bill of Entry, which is not a New Zealand statutory document

Bill of Lading for sea cargo or air waybill/master air waybill for air cargo evidencing physical export from New Zealand, endorsed by the carrier, together with commercial invoice, packing list, and Customs-approved commodity/valuation data

Bank statement or SWIFT payment confirmation evidencing receipt of the foreign-currency or New Zealand-dollar remittance from the offshore buyer into the New Zealand entity's bank account, together with the underlying sales contract and records required by the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009; New Zealand does not issue an Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC), and the bank payment record is the accepted foreign-exchange repatriation evidence
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: New Zealand legislation does not impose a fixed 180-day export-proceeds repatriation deadline; the 180-day value in this dossier is the audit-readiness benchmark, and longer deferrals require documented commercial justification. Inland Revenue may challenge export zero-rating if the documentation bundle is incomplete or inconsistent, or if the goods or services are later returned to, restored to, or consumed in New Zealand. Retrospective GST clawback arises if physical export or qualifying offshore service is not substantiated: the supply is reassessed at 15% GST and input credits previously allowed on related costs may be adjusted. Penalties include GST shortfall, use-of-money interest from the original due date, late-filing penalties, graduated shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 from failure to take reasonable care through abusive tax positions and evasion, and criminal prosecution for intentionally false documents or fraudulent zero-rating claims. The standard four-year reassessment period applies to non-fraudulent supplies, with no statutory time bar for fraud or evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand operates a free-floating and fully convertible currency regime. The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is freely traded in global markets, with no foreign exchange controls, capital account restrictions, or exchange surrender requirements imposed by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand. Current account transactions such as software export receipts, dividends, royalties, and service fees may be settled freely in NZD or any convertible currency. Capital account transactions, including direct equity investment, internal corporate loans, and repatriation of invested capital, are likewise unrestricted and do not require Exchange Control approval. The principal gateways are bank-level AML/CFT and sanctions due diligence, any applicable tax clearance for dividends or interest payments under New Zealand tax law, and the Overseas Investment Act 2005, which may screen certain non-resident acquisitions of significant business assets or farm land; a vertical SaaS company selling software services does not ordinarily trigger that regime. Profit remittance can be executed by instructing the bank to convert NZD to the target currency at a wholesale rate and issue a SWIFT MT103, or by remitting directly in NZD where the beneficiary can accept that currency. There is no prescription requiring a minimum local holding period, no forced conversion, and no black-market premium because official and market rates are identical. The real-time settlement infrastructure for NZD is the Exchange Settlement Account System operated by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand, while cross-border settlements clear through correspondent banks and SWIFT. In practice, the only hurdles are documentary: source-of-funds evidence, clean corporate ownership, and alignment with the bank's risk appetite.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. New Zealand does not impose statutory timelines or mandatory conversion ratios for export foreign currency receipts. Exporters may maintain foreign currency bank accounts offshore or with domestic banks, retain export proceeds indefinitely, and buy or sell NZD freely. For tax, exporters report accrual income in NZD using the applicable exchange rate, but this is a tax translation measure, not a surrender rule. If a transaction is processed through a domestic bank and exceeds the Financial Transaction Reporting threshold, standard AML/CFT record-keeping and, where applicable, suspicious transaction reporting apply.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech EMIs are viable but require registration on New Zealand's Financial Service Providers Register and compliance with the AML/CFT Act 2009. An offshore fintech EMI without a local Financial Service Providers Register linkage cannot lawfully provide payment services directly to a New Zealand entity. If the EMI operates through a local partner bank or is an approved non-bank payment provider, it may offer multicurrency collections and disbursements, but the underlying settlement is still supported by a registered New Zealand bank. For core treasury and capital escrow functions, a Tier-1 domestic bank is strongly preferred; an EMI may be used as a secondary collection rail for Stripe Billing and Direct Debit if it can demonstrate a valid local registration, client fund segregation, and clear audit trail. Overall feasibility rating: cautious supplementary use rather than primary banking infrastructure.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no statutory requirement for every director to attend in-branch; remote electronic identity verification is permissible under the AML/CFT Act 2009 using an New Zealand-regulated verification provider. In practice, the account opening entity must be registered in New Zealand and must provide a board resolution, proof of registered office, and identification of all directors and beneficial owners. Most major banks allow a video interview with the director or principal owner, supported by certified copies of passports and a notarized utility bill. A pure consular proxy opening with no direct contact is unlikely to be accepted because the bank must conduct its own risk assessment; however, a director located overseas can generally open the account remotely through the bank's international onboarding desk. For any increased-risk element, an in-branch interview may be mandated at the bank's discretion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owner with a complex multi-layer corporate structure that obscures the ultimate natural person owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate registry extracts for the New Zealand company and every intermediate holding entity; trust deed if any trust is involved; certificates of incorporation; board resolution authorising account opening; organisational chart showing the complete ownership chain; source-of-wealth statement signed by each non-resident shareholder; tax residency certificates and IRD numbers or foreign equivalent; six months of bank statements for the remitting entity; and independent sanctions and adverse-media screening reports.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial inbound equity capital originating from a jurisdiction outside the bank's ordinary correspondent banking network or from a higher-risk jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-funds dossier including audited financial statements of the remitting shareholder; commercial contracts and invoice trail supporting the software revenue; historical SWIFT transaction records; tax payment receipts in the source jurisdiction; notarised legal opinion from local counsel confirming lawful origin; a detailed narrative of how the capital was accumulated; confirmation that the shareholder is not a PEP unless cleared; and a bank-to-bank confirmation from the remitting institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained high-velocity payment flow where the ERP/CRM billing remitters do not clearly match the company's declared customer base.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed KYC questionnaire mapping each contracted client to the actual remitter; signed master subscription or software licence agreements; cloud architecture and service delivery documentation; data processing agreements; customer due diligence files for any reseller or distributor; payment reconciliation report generated from Stripe Billing and Direct Debit rails; explanation of any third-party settlement arrangements; and a letter from the local registered accountant confirming the commercial substance of the revenue stream.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: A director or beneficial owner identified as a politically exposed person or holding a conflicting foreign government role.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due diligence questionnaire; independent PEP database screening; source of funds and source of wealth statement; official government employment or resignation records; sanctions clearance; notarised identity and address documents; senior management approval memorandum from the bank; and a professional reference from a New Zealand-registered lawyer or chartered accountant.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The shareholder or parent entity should route equity injections via SWIFT MT103 from the remitting bank to the company's designated capital account in New Zealand. In Field 70, the payment narrative should clearly state SHARE CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION or EQUITY INJECTION. If using ISO 20022 purpose codes, apply EQUI for equity or CAPI for capital injection. Because New Zealand does not operate a capital verification bureau, the company must maintain its own statutory capital register and reconcile the bank credit advice against the board resolution allotting shares, the shareholder subscription agreement, and the company register. The receiving bank may request a declaration of source of funds and, for material amounts, a Banker's Confirmation from the remitting institution. There is no requirement to convert inbound foreign currency to NZD; the company may retain the funds in the currency received or convert through the bank's FX desk at a wholesale rate. All inbound credits must be matched to the approved account structure to avoid triggering AML alerts.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements, use SWIFT MT103 for direct cash payment of invoices for software licences, hosted cloud services, subcontracting, and subscription fees; use irrevocable Commercial Letters of Credit via MT700 for physical goods procurement or large capital investments if the seller requires bank payment assurance; and use Documentary Collections on a documents-against-payment or documents-against-acceptance basis for low-risk, long-established counterparties. NZD-denominated vendor payments clear through the Exchange Settlement Account System, while multi-currency disbursements clear through the bank's global correspondent network. Each outbound wire must carry a purpose code consistent with the underlying commercial contract and be supported by an invoice, statement of work, or contract schedule. For recurring global cloud-hosting fees, a standing payment instruction with quarterly auto-reconciliation is acceptable, but the bank should receive the annual contract schedule to avoid transaction monitoring delays.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward foreign exchange contracts for NZD versus USD, AUD, EUR, GBP, and major Asian currencies with tenors typically up to 24 months
FX swaps and cross-currency interest rate swaps used to hedge intercompany loan principal and interest exposures
Vanilla FX options, zero-cost collars, and participating forwards for cash-flow protection

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) may be executed only with a licensed bank and only where a deliverable forward is impossible; because NZD is fully convertible, deliverable forwards are the standard instrument and NDFs are rarely necessary

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of a New Zealand Limited Company (Companies Act 1993, s209)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one calendar month after the company's statutory 'return date', which is the anniversary of incorporation or the anniversary of the immediately preceding annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a Companies Office reminder and, if unresolved, an infringement notice (NZD 500 approx. USD 305). Persistent default enables the Registrar to propose removal of the company from the New Zealand Register under s318 of the Companies Act 1993 after a Gazette notice and a 20 working day objection window. Each director may additionally be prosecuted and fined up to NZD 10,000 (approx. USD 6,100). Dissolution follows actual removal, causing loss of limited liability and vesting of company assets in the Crown.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements Filing for Large or FMC Reporting Entities (Financial Reporting Act 2013)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies), MBIE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March balance date, financial statements must be completed and delivered to shareholders within 5 months (31 August) for FMC reporting entities, and within 9 months (31 December) for other large companies; when filing with the Companies Office, the same filing deadlines under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 apply
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare, audit, or file financial statements when statutorily required is an offence punishable by a director's fine of up to NZD 10,000, and for continuing non-compliance up to NZD 50,000 per director. The Registrar may also treat the failure as grounds for removal under s318 of the Companies Act 1993. An audit report qualification or non-filing may trigger automatic review by the Registrar of statutory compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (IR4 Company Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For companies with a 31 March balance date, the IR4 is due by 7 July following the end of the tax year; with a tax agent extension, the due date is the following 31 March. For a non-standard balance date, the return is generally due on the 28th day of the 7th month after balance date, or the extended 31 March for tax agents
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty NZD 250 (approx. USD 152); late payment penalties of 1% on day one, 4% after seven days, and 1% per month thereafter; statutory interest accrues daily at IRD's prescribed rate. Continued tax default may trigger a default assessment, salary/property deductions, and the Registrar could later strike off the company for persistently failing to meet statutory obligations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual GST Return (if the company uses the annual GST filing option or has a six-monthly GST cycle ending at balance date)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 March balance date, the GST period ending on 31 March is due for filing by 28 April (or 28th day of the month following the end of the GST taxable period) if the company files annually or six-monthly
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty NZD 250 (approx. USD 152); late payment penalties and interest as prescribed by IRD, including a 1% initial penalty, 4% additional penalty after seven days, and 1% monthly. IRD may issue a default assessment and collect debts through enforcement, and continuing non-compliance can contribute to a company strike-off action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Fringe Benefit Tax Return (IR420) - only if the company provides fringe benefits to employees
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For the standard 31 March tax year, the annual FBT return is due by 7 July (with agent extension to 31 March); quarter-end FBT filing is due on the 28th day of the month after the quarter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty NZD 250 (approx. USD 152) plus late payment penalties and interest at IRD prescribed rates. Failure to comply can result in assessment, penalty tax, and Crown enforcement measures, including garnishment of bank accounts and potential corporate strike-off if the company is habitually non-compliant.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, an independent statutory audit is mandatory for (i) any New Zealand company that qualifies as a 'large' company - i.e., it exceeds at least one of the following thresholds in both the current and the immediately preceding accounting period: (a) total assets at balance date exceed NZD 60 million; (b) total revenue for the period exceeds NZD 30 million; (c) the company has 50 or more full-time equivalent employees; (ii) any FMC reporting entity under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, including issuers of listed equity/debt, managed investment scheme managers, and companies offering securities to the public; and (iii) any company whose shareholders holding not less than 5% of the voting shares or the Registrar validly request an audit in writing. Where any such threshold is met, the audit must be performed by a licensed statutory auditor in accordance with the Auditor Regulation Act 2011 and the professional assurance standards published by the External Reporting Board.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting practice (GAAP) in New Zealand as defined by the Financial Reporting Act 2013. For public benefit entities and large for-profit entities, the framework is New Zealand Equivalents to International Financial Reporting Standards (NZ IFRS). Non-publicly accountable entities may apply the NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime (NZ IFRS RDR), and very small entities may use the New Zealand Simplified Accounting Standard (NZSAS). Financial statements must be accompanied by an auditor's report for entities above the statutory audit thresholds.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Companies (Beneficial Ownership Information) Amendment Act 2023, every New Zealand company must maintain an accurate beneficial ownership register and confirm beneficial ownership information to the Registrar of Companies on each Annual Return. Any transfer of shares or other change resulting in a change of beneficial ownership must be reported to the New Zealand Companies Office within 30 days of the change, and the company's internal register of beneficial ownership must be updated no later than the date on which the change occurs. For ordinary share transfers that do not change beneficial ownership, the transfer must still be recorded in the Register of Members without any Government filing; a separate notice of allotment is required only for new share allotments, which must be filed within 10 working days under s187 of the Companies Act 1993. The annual confirmation must state the name, date of birth, address, and nature of control or ownership of every significant beneficial owner.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - USD 15,000 per audit engagement depending on company size, complexity, and the appointed CAANZ licensed auditor

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Research and Development Tax Incentive (RDTI) at 20% of eligible R&D expenditure (15% for expenditure incurred before 1 April 2024); no patent box or free-zone concession is available; tax losses may be carried forward indefinitely subject to the shareholder continuity rules (49% ownership continuity for offset against a shareholder's income and 66% for carry-forward between accounting periods).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 Company Income Tax Return filed electronically through the Inland Revenue myIR online portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The IR4 must be filed by the 7th day of the fourth month following the company's balance date; for a standard 31 March balance date the filing deadline is 7 July in the same income year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company legal name, IRD number, and registered office address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact name registered with the New Zealand Companies Office; disclose the ultimate foreign shareholder and any New Zealand permanent establishment of the non-resident parent to avoid an incorrect imputation or NRWT assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance date and accounting period covered by the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm the standard 31 March balance date or a substituted balance date approved by Inland Revenue. The return period must reconcile with the statutory accounts; any change of balance date triggered by a foreign parent's consolidation cycle requires prior approval.

Include all New Zealand-source income: SaaS subscription fees, licence revenue, maintenance fees, and cloud services. Recharacterise any software payment that constitutes a royalty for use of IT software. Cross-border recharging to the overseas parent must be confirmed at arm's length before reporting.

Claim ordinary and R&D expenses, cloud infrastructure cost, and employee wages. Deny deductions for intercompany management fees or royalties that are not supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation and service benefit tests; apply the strict thin capitalisation rules for any debt funding from non-resident shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income or net loss before tax loss offset.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute the assessable income minus allowable deductions. A net loss must be quarantined if the company fails continuity of ownership (49% test) or business continuity is broken, which is common when a foreign investor acquires the NZ Ltd.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses offset and final net taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Offset carried-forward losses only where the 66% shareholder continuity is maintained. The resulting taxable income is then multiplied by the 28% corporate tax rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits: resident withholding tax, provisional tax paid, foreign tax credits, and R&D tax credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim the RDTI credit at 20% of eligible R&D, RWT credits on interest/dividends, and foreign tax credits for overseas income. Imputation credits cannot be transferred to non-resident shareholders and may be refundable only in limited circumstances.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Residual income tax payable or refund due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay the residual amount by the terminal due date (generally 7 July for 31 March balance dates); any underpayment attracts interest under s. 120 of the Tax Administration Act 1994 and the non-resident shareholder's dividend repatriation will be subject to NRWT on the payment of dividends.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the IR4 triggers an initial late filing penalty of NZ$250 (NZ$500 for large taxpayers) plus NZ$50 per day for each day the return remains outstanding, capped at NZ$1,000. Late payment of residual income tax attracts an immediate 1% first-stage late payment penalty, followed by a 4% quarterly second-stage penalty accumulating over time. Deliberate filing of a false or misleading IR4 is a criminal offence under section 143A/143B of the Tax Administration Act 1994, punishable by a fine up to NZ$150,000 (company) or NZ$75,000 (individual) and a term of imprisonment up to three years; civil shortfall penalties up to 150% of the resulting tax shortfall are also imposed.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) on non-imputed dividends paid to non-resident shareholders; 15% NRWT on fully imputed dividends when the dividend is fully imputed and the 15% rate is elected.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The mandatory administrative protocol to apply a reduced DTA rate is: (1) the non-resident recipient obtains a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its jurisdiction of residence; (2) the New Zealand payer must receive a signed IR290 declaration (notice of NRWT reduction) or a valid exemption certificate before the payment date; (3) the recipient must provide documentary evidence of beneficial ownership, including legal and corporate structure documentation and evidence of economic substance in the residence jurisdiction; (4) the payer applies the reduced treaty rate at source on the payment date; and (5) all documents must be retained for at least seven years. Typical treaty rates for dividends range from 0% to 15% (e.g., 15% under the NZ-Australia DTA with portfolio holdings), while the NZ-Hong Kong DTA grants 0% on dividends where a resident NZ company holds at least 80% of the Hong Kong recipient; royalties are generally reduced to 10% and interest to 10% under most NZ DTAs.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT is 15% on gross royalties and 15% on gross interest; an Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) of 2% can be substituted for NRWT on interest paid by an approved issuer. For software arrangements, payments for standardised cloud/SaaS subscriptions ordinarily constitute business profits (no NRWT), while payments for the use of copyright in software constitute royalties (NRWT 15%, treaty-reduced frequently to 10%). Interest treaty rates range from 0% to 10% depending on the DTA partner.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NZ$10 million aggregated cross-border related-party transactions per income year; where the threshold is exceeded, the taxpayer must prepare contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation (Local File/Master File equivalent) and be able to provide it to Inland Revenue within 30 days of a request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not maintain a separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) statute comparable to the UAE, but the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) in section BG 1 of the Income Tax Act 2007 and the doctrines of 'sham' and 'substance over form' enforce an economic substance requirement. A New Zealand Ltd must perform Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) locally—including management, contract negotiation, and risk control—in order to retain treaty benefits, secure imputation credits, and avoid the recharacterisation of arrangements by Inland Revenue.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully omitting SaaS subscription revenue or inflating intercompany deductions in the IR4 to shift profit to an offshore related party, including backdating invoices for software development services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Sections 143A-143C of the Tax Administration Act 1994: evasion of tax is punishable by a fine not exceeding NZ$150,000 for a company and/or a director; individuals face a fine not exceeding NZ$75,000 and/or imprisonment up to three years. A civil shortfall penalty of 100% of the tax shortfall is also imposed under section 141D.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced where a director signs or directly participates in the false return; the director is jointly and severally liable for the tax shortfall, faces asset recovery actions, a High Court travel ban (asset freezing and departure prohibition) under section 173A of the Tax Administration Act, and criminal imprisonment of up to three years, plus disqualification from holding a directorship under the Companies Act 1993.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a New Zealand Ltd with no employees, premises, or decision-making functions solely as a conduit to access New Zealand's Double Tax Agreement network and to obtain reduced NRWT rates on dividends, interest, and royalties flowing to a foreign parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The arrangement is void under section BG 1 (GAAR) and is recharacterised under section GB 1 of the Income Tax Act 2007; a 40% shortfall penalty applies for an abusive tax position under section 141A, plus use-of-money interest, and the denied treaty benefits result in the full 30% NRWT on dividends and 15% NRWT on royalties/interests being reassessed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who benefit from or control the unreal activity are personally liable for the recovered tax shortfall under section 34 of the Tax Administration Act, exposing personal assets, a travel ban (blacklisting) for the unpaid amount, and criminal prosecution for aiding in tax evasion under section 143A, carrying imprisonment of up to three years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to implement a risk-based AML/CFT programme and refusing to file suspicious transaction reports while processing large cross-border software revenue through payment rails such as Stripe Billing and Direct Debit, thereby knowingly facilitating money laundering or terrorist financing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Sections 89 and 90 of the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009: a company is liable to a civil penalty not exceeding NZ$1 million for each contravention; directors and officers are liable to a penalty not exceeding NZ$250,000 and/or imprisonment for a term not exceeding two years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced on proof of a director's knowledge or wilful blindness; directors face criminal conviction with imprisonment up to two years, personal fines, asset restraining orders, travel bans, and disqualification from managing companies under the Financial Markets Authority enforcement regime.
